title: Recent or distant?
theme: Present perfect vs past simple — when to use each
goal: Student distinguishes PP (life experience, connected to present) from past simple (finished time), and uses for/since correctly.
connects_to: M04 (used to) — after mastering PP, learn past habits.
module_chunks: for + duration (for two years, for an hour)
since + point in time (since 2010, since Monday)

units.title: Finished or still going?
units.grammar_focus: PP for connected past vs past simple for finished
units.real_life_context: You distinguish what's finished from what's still relevant.

grammar.explanation: "Last year" = finished time → past simple. "I visited Italy last year".

grammar.sentence: I _____ Italy three times in my life.
grammar.explanation: "In my life" = experience, no specific time → present perfect.
"This morning" (if it's still morning) = unfinished → PP. If morning is over → past simple "called".

grammar.sentence: I _____ him in 2010 and I _____ him many times since.
grammar.explanation: "In 2010" = specific past → "met". (Second blank would be "have seen/met").
"Ago" always with past simple. "Visited Brazil three years ago".
"Yesterday" = specific finished time → past simple, not PP.

grammar.sentence: I visited many countries in my life.
grammar.answer: I have visited many countries in my life.
grammar.explanation: "In my life" = no specific time, experience → PP.

grammar.passage: I went to Italy last year. I've visited it three times in my life. I haven't been there yet this year.
grammar.question: When did the speaker go to Italy specifically?
grammar.explanation: The text says "I went to Italy last year".

listening_speaking.text: I visited Italy last year.
I have visited Italy three times.
She called yesterday.
She has called this morning.
We met in 2010.

roleplay.scenario: Charlotte asks about experiences and specific past events.
roleplay.opening_line: Tell me about a past trip — and a life experience.

objectives.hidden_prompt: user uses past simple with time marker (last year, yesterday, in 2020)
objectives.hint_en: I went to Italy last year.
examples_pass: I went to Italy last year.

objectives.hidden_prompt: user uses 'I have + past participle' for life experience
user uses one more past simple or PP with appropriate marker

roleplay.closing_cue: Charlotte closes with "Good distinction!" when obj_3 hits.
roleplay.suggested_flow:
**Suggested flow** (referential, 6 turns):

1. **Charlotte**: "Tell me about a past trip — and a life experience."
2. **Student**: ~"I went to Italy last year."
3. **Charlotte**: "Lifetime experiences?"
4. **Student**: ~"I have visited five countries."
5. **Charlotte**: "Anything never tried?"
6. **Student**: ~"I have never tried sushi."
7. **Charlotte**: "Good distinction!"
evaluation_focus: Time markers correctly paired (yesterday → simple, ever → PP)

guided_chat.scenario: Charlotte chats about distinguishing past tenses.
guided_chat.intro_en: Charlotte asks about finished events vs life experiences. Practice the distinction.
guided_chat.opening_message: Specific past event — what did you do last weekend?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user uses past simple with specific time
objectives.hint_en: I traveled to Rio last weekend.
examples_pass: I traveled to Rio last weekend.

objectives.hidden_prompt: user uses PP for life experience
user asks specific or experience question
objectives.hint_en: Have you ever been to Brazil?
examples_pass: Have you ever been to Brazil?

guided_chat.closing_cue: Charlotte closes with "Tense mastery!" when obj_3 hits.
guided_chat.suggested_script:
**Script** (referential, 7 turns):

1. **Charlotte**: "Specific past event — what did you do last weekend?"
2. **Student**: "I traveled to Rio last weekend."
3. **Charlotte**: "Lifetime?"
4. **Student**: "I've traveled a lot."
5. **Charlotte**: "Lucky."
6. **Student**: "Have you ever been to Brazil?"
7. **Charlotte**: "Yes! Tense mastery!"

> I01 chat = LLM puro.

units.title: For two years
units.real_life_context: You describe duration of ongoing situations.

grammar.sentence: I have lived here _____ two years.
grammar.explanation: "For + duration" — period of time. "For two years".

grammar.sentence: She has worked there _____ a long time.
He has had this car _____ five years.
I have studied English _____ two years.
She has known him _____ a long time.

grammar.explanation: "How long have you lived here?" — common question.

grammar.sentence: I have lived here since two years.
grammar.hint: Since for point in time, not duration
grammar.answer: I have lived here for two years.
grammar.explanation: "Since" is for point (since 2020). "For" is for duration (for 2 years).

grammar.sentence: "I lived here for two years." (still living there)
grammar.answer: I have lived here for two years.
grammar.explanation: If still living = PP. Past simple = finished.

grammar.passage: I have lived in São Paulo for ten years. I've worked at my company for five years. My sister has studied English for three years.
grammar.question: How long has the sister studied English?

listening_speaking.text: I've lived here for two years.
She has worked there for a long time.
We've been friends for years.
How long have you lived here?
He has had this car for five years.

units.title: Since 2010
units.real_life_context: You anchor situations to a starting point.

grammar.explanation: "Since + point in time" (2010, Monday, last year).

grammar.sentence: He has lived here _____ he was 10.
grammar.explanation: "Since" can introduce a clause: "since he was 10" — starting point.

grammar.sentence: I have lived here _____ I was born.
grammar.explanation: "Since I was born" — starting reference point.
"How long have you been waiting?" — duration question.

grammar.sentence: I have lived here since two years.
grammar.answer: I have lived here for two years.
grammar.explanation: "Two years" = duration → "for". "Since" needs a point in time.
"Since" + PP. Present simple doesn't work with since.

grammar.passage: I have lived here since 2015. I have worked at this company since January. My best friend and I have been friends since school.
grammar.question: Since when has the speaker worked at this company?

listening_speaking.text: I've known her since 2010.
She has worked since January.
We've been here since 9 am.
He has lived here since he was 10.
How long have you been here?

roleplay.scenario: Charlotte asks about starting points in your life.
roleplay.opening_line: Tell me three things you've been doing — since when?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user uses 'I've + past participle + since + year'
user uses 'since + month/day'
user uses 'since + clause' (since I was..., since I moved...)
objectives.hint_en: I've lived here since I was 18.
examples_pass: I've lived here since I was 18.

roleplay.closing_cue: Charlotte closes with "Anchored in time!" when obj_3 hits.
roleplay.suggested_flow:
**Suggested flow** (referential, 6 turns):

1. **Charlotte**: "Tell me three things you've been doing — since when?"
2. **Student**: ~"I've worked here since 2020."
3. **Charlotte**: "Recent?"
4. **Student**: ~"I've been busy since Monday."
5. **Charlotte**: "Longest?"
6. **Student**: ~"I've lived here since I was 18."
7. **Charlotte**: "Anchored in time!"

guided_chat.intro_en: Charlotte asks since when. Practice 'since + point'.
guided_chat.opening_message: Since when have you studied English?

objectives.hidden_prompt: user uses 'since + point'
user uses 'I've + past participle + since'
user asks 'Since when have you...?'

units.title: How long have you?
units.real_life_context: You ask and answer about durations of ongoing situations.

grammar.explanation: "How long" for duration questions in PP.

grammar.sentence: I've been here _____ a few minutes.
How long do you live here?
grammar.answer: How long have you lived here?
grammar.explanation: For ongoing situations (still living), use PP "have lived".

grammar.sentence: I have been here from one hour.
grammar.answer: I have been here for one hour.

grammar.passage: Q: How long have you lived in São Paulo? A: For ten years. Q: Since when have you worked there? A: Since 2020.
grammar.question: Since when has the person worked there?

listening_speaking.text: How long have you lived here?
How long has she known him?
How long have they been together?
I've been here for a few minutes.
Since when have you worked here?

units.title: Past or perfect?
units.grammar_focus: Integration past simple vs present perfect
units.real_life_context: You combine both tenses naturally in conversation.

grammar.sentence: "She _____ already." (sooner than expected, no specific time)
I _____ her in 2010 and we _____ best friends since.
grammar.explanation: "In 2010" = past simple "met". Second part would be "have been".

grammar.sentence: "He _____ five books this year." (year not finished)
I visited five countries in my life.
grammar.answer: I have visited five countries in my life.

grammar.passage: I went to Italy in 2019. I've been there twice in my life. I haven't traveled this year. I saw an old friend last month.
grammar.question: When did the speaker see the old friend?
grammar.explanation: The text says "I saw an old friend last month".

listening_speaking.text: I visited Italy last year.
I have visited Italy three times.
She left at 8.
She has already left.
I haven't traveled this year.
